key_insight: In metal-halide perovskites, hyperfine-driven spin relaxation is highly asymmetric: electrons mainly couple to halogen nuclei, while holes couple to metal nuclei, making exact dynamical modeling necessary when spin correlation times are intermediate.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and tuning hyperfine interactions can help engineer perovskite compositions with longer carrier spin lifetimes, which may benefit spintronic and optoelectronic device performance.
method: Adapted a muon spin relaxation model to localized charge carriers in perovskites.
Solved longitudinal spin relaxation exactly across arbitrary hyperfine correlation times.
Compared the model with time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two perovskite samples to extract localization volume and correlation time.
evidence_signal: The model was applied to time-resolved Faraday rotation measurements on two perovskite samples and showed that a single-exponential approximation is insufficient in the intermediate correlation regime.
watch_item: The results rely on localized-carrier assumptions and accurate knowledge of hyperfine correlation time, so the model may need revalidation for highly delocalized or strongly disordered materials.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
